issues.legal_issue: A levy calculated by tea despatches, rather than by characteristics of the tea estate, directly restricts the movement of goods and is invalid when the required constitutional procedure for such a restriction was not followed.
material_facts: The levy was calculated by the weight of tea despatched from an estate.
The statutory scheme allowed different treatment depending on the class of tea and, initially, the destination or sale centre of the despatches.
The Court found no relationship between that differential treatment and the tea estate that was ostensibly the subject of the levy.
The amendments introducing the levy were not moved in the State Legislature with the President’s previous sanction.
issues.conclusion: In substance, the levy was on tea despatches and directly restricted the flow of trade and commerce. Because the amendments lacked the President’s previous sanction, the impugned provisions were unconstitutional and void.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 301, a tax violates the freedom of trade if it directly and immediately impedes the movement of goods; an indirect or remote effect does not suffice. Article 304(b) permits reasonable restrictions required in the public interest, but its proviso requires the President’s previous sanction for the Bill or amendment. The true subject of a levy must be identified from the substance of the legislation, distinguishing the subject of the levy from the measure of liability. The measure must have a nexus with the subject. The Court relied on Atiabari Tea Co. Ltd. v. State of Assam, The Automobile Transport (Rajasthan) Ltd. v. State of Rajasthan, Firm A.T.B. Mehtab Majid and Company v. State of Madras, Kalyani Stores v. State of Orissa, State of Mysore v. H. Sanjeeviah, Andhra Sugars Ltd. v. State of Andhra Pradesh, Union of India v. Bombay Tyre International Ltd., Re: A Reference under the Government of Ireland Act, R.R. Engineering Co. v. Zila Parishad, Bareilly, and Hingir-Rampur Coal Co. Ltd. v. State of Orissa.

rule.if: constitutional_challenge_to_state_levy and levy_calculated_by_quantity_dispatched and differential_treatment_turns_on_tea_class_or_sale_destination and no_nexus_between_differential_treatment_and_estate and not prior_presidential_sanction

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_state_levy: The proceeding challenges the constitutional validity of a State-imposed levy.
predicates.levy_calculated_by_quantity_dispatched: The State calculated the levy by the quantity of goods dispatched from an estate.
predicates.differential_treatment_turns_on_tea_clas: The State provided different rates or exemptions according to the class of goods or their sale destination.
predicates.no_nexus_between_differential_treatment_: The State’s differing treatment of dispatches had no demonstrated relationship to the characteristics of the estate made the subject of the levy.
predicates.prior_presidential_sanction: The Bill or amendment imposing the restriction was introduced or moved in the State Legislature with the President’s previous sanction.

issues.definition: When a constitutional challenge concerns a State levy calculated by the quantity of goods dispatched, and differential treatment lacks a connection to the ostensible estate subject while the required prior sanction is absent, the levy is an unconstitutional direct restriction on trade.

issues.legal_issue: A State lacks legislative competence to impose a levy on tea despatches where the subject falls within an industry and trade field placed under Union control and no supporting State or Concurrent List entry is identified.
material_facts: The Court determined that the levy was in substance imposed on tea despatches, not on tea estates or land.
Parliament had declared that Union control of the tea industry was expedient in the public interest and had assumed control of the industry, including tea trade and prices.
Parliament had also imposed a cess on tea produced in India.
No relevant entry in the State List or Concurrent List was shown to support the State levy.
issues.conclusion: The impugned legislation was also void for want of legislative competence because it pertained to a field under Union control.
issues.legal_principle: A levy must be supported by legislative authority over its true subject matter. Although a levy on estates could fall under Entry 49 of List II, this levy was in substance on tea despatches. Parliament had assumed control of the tea industry under sections 2 and 25 of the Tea Act, 1953, including the trade in tea and tea prices, and no pertinent State or Concurrent List entry supported the levy.

predicates.challenge_to_state_levy: The proceeding challenges a levy imposed by a State.
predicates.levy_in_substance_concerns_goods_dispatc: The levy, considered in substance, applies to the dispatch of goods rather than to land or an estate.
predicates.parliament_declared_union_control_of_ind: Parliament declared Union control over the industry and exercised control over its trade.
predicates.no_relevant_state_or_concurrent_entry_wa: No legislative entry supporting the State levy was identified in the State or Concurrent List.

issues.definition: When a challenged State levy concerns goods dispatches within an industry and trade subject to declared Union control, and no relevant State or Concurrent List authority is shown, the State levy exceeds legislative competence.

issues.legal_issue: Persons who paid a levy imposed under provisions declared void are entitled to a refund of the amounts paid.
material_facts: The petitioners paid cess under the impugned statutory provisions.
The Court declared those provisions void insofar as they purported to relate to tea estates.
issues.conclusion: The petitioners were entitled to a refund of the cess paid under the impugned provisions.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the petitioners who had paid the cess under the provisions it declared void were entitled to a refund; it relied on no separate earlier case for this relief.

predicates.proceeding_challenges_levy: The proceeding challenges the validity of a levy.
predicates.payer_paid_under_provisions_declared_voi: The payer paid the levy under provisions that the court declared void.

issues.definition: A payer who challenges a levy and paid it under provisions declared void is entitled to a refund.
